title: What to do with Mamasapano dismissals
primary_topics: Sandiganbayan's Jan 21, 2020 dismissal (without trial) of two criminal charges against former PNP chief Alan Purisima and former SAF director Getulio Napeñas in connection with the Mamasapano Massacre
Doctrinal basis 1: 'failure to allege a crime' under Section 3(a) of the Anti-Graft Law (no allegation of 'any material remuneration or consideration')

stances.claim: The Sandiganbayan's Jan 21, 2020 dismissal (Justice Quiroz ponente, Cruz and Musngi concurring) rests on two doctrinal grounds: (1) the Anti-Graft Law information failed to allege a crime because it did not allege that Purisima and Napeñas received or expected 'material remuneration or consideration' for the prohibited acts; and (2) the usurpation-of-official-functions information lacked probable cause because Purisima, though suspended, was merely following President Aquino's direct orders as CinC.
stances.rhetorical_move: doctrinal-summary register identifying the two pillars of the dismissal

stances.claim: Justice Bayani H. Jacinto's dissent is doctrinally correct on the Anti-Graft Law point: 'material remuneration or consideration' under Section 3(a) is required only when the inducement does not involve the commission of a crime -- not when, as here, the inducement involves the commission of acts amounting to a crime; and Presiding Justice Cabotaje-Tang's partial dissent on the usurpation count is also doctrinally well-grounded since the constitutive elements were sufficiently alleged.
stances.rhetorical_move: doctrinal-sympathy stance with the dissenters without overruling the result
stances.confidence: asserted by report and implicit endorsement

stances.claim: The pragmatic choice for the OMB and SAF 44 lies between (a) motion for reconsideration + SC appeal to obtain clear jurisprudence (with likely remand to SBN for trial and possible second SC appeal), and (b) accepting the SBN ruling and refiling appropriate charges per the SBN's own 'without prejudice' caveat -- a multi-year vs more-immediate-action trade-off.
stances.rhetorical_move: decision-tree taxonomy laying out the two doctrinal paths

stances.claim: Given that the Mamasapano Massacre is already five years past, the informations are two years old, and only a dismissal resolution has been produced, the risk of further delay -- witnesses disappearing, memories faltering, evidence misplaced, public support diminished -- makes it more prudent to accept the SBN resolution, refile 'appropriate charges,' and let the lively legal debate of the SBN justices be resolved in another case. Speedy justice for the SAF 44 should take precedence over clear jurisprudence on Section 3(a) of the Anti-Graft Law.

notable_anecdotes: The fractured 3-1-1 composition of the Sandiganbayan resolution: Justices Quiroz, Cruz, and Musngi forming the majority; Justice Jacinto dissenting on the Anti-Graft Law construction; Presiding Justice Cabotaje-Tang agreeing on the Anti-Graft Law but dissenting on the usurpation count -- used by CJ as an empirical demonstration that the doctrine is genuinely contested at the SBN level.

The dismissal's 'without prejudice to the filing of the appropriate charge/s' caveat -- the doctrinal hinge that makes the pragmatic alternative viable and that CJ uses as the operative escape valve from years of further SC review.

The temporal accumulation that anchors the speedy-justice argument: the Mamasapano Massacre happened five years ago, the informations were filed two years ago, the SBN produced only a dismissal resolution -- and a motion-for-reconsideration / SC-appeal path would consume several more years before any conviction could be remanded back to the SBN for trial.

The roll call of erosion risks if the SAF 44 endure the longer doctrinal path -- 'some witnesses may disappear, their memories may falter, the evidence may be misplaced, and public support diminished' -- a quietly grim taxonomy of how delay erodes accountability.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban analyzes the Sandiganbayan's Jan 21, 2020 outright dismissal -- 'without trial and reception of evidence' -- of the two criminal charges against former PNP chief Alan Purisima and former PNP SAF director Getulio Napeñas in connection with the Mamasapano Massacre that killed 44 SAF officers. The 18-page resolution penned by Justice Alex L. Quiroz (concurred in by Justices Reynaldo P. Cruz and Michael Frederick L. Musngi) rests on two grounds: (1) the Anti-Graft Law information under Section 3(a) failed to allege a crime because it did not allege that the accused received or expected 'any material remuneration or consideration' for the prohibited acts; and (2) the usurpation-of-official-functions information lacked probable cause because Purisima -- though suspended by the OMB -- was merely following the direct orders of then-President Benigno Aquino III as CinC, who in turn ordered Purisima to supervise the planning and execution of 'Oplan Exodus' and whose own parallel charges had already been dismissed by the SBN. The SBN held that proceeding to arrest and trial was pointless because even if proven, no conviction was possible, though the dismissal was 'without prejudice to the filing of the appropriate charge/s.' Justice Bayani H. Jacinto dissented on the Anti-Graft Law point, arguing that 'material remuneration or consideration' is required only when the inducement does not involve the commission of a crime -- not when, as here, the inducement involves the commission of acts amounting to a crime. Presiding Justice Amparo M. Cabotaje-Tang agreed with the majority on the Anti-Graft Law dismissal but dissented on the usurpation count, holding that the constitutive elements were sufficiently alleged. CJ frames the strategic question: should the OMB and the SAF 44 ask for reconsideration and ultimately appeal to the SC for clear jurisprudence (with likely remand to the SBN for trial and possible second SC appeal -- adding several more years), or should they accept the SBN ruling and refile 'appropriate charges' per the without-prejudice caveat? Given that the Massacre is already five years past, the informations are two years old, and the long doctrinal path risks witness disappearance, faltering memories, misplaced evidence, and diminished public support, CJ argues it is more prudent to accept the SBN resolution, let the lively legal debate of the SBN justices be resolved in another case, and let speedy justice be done to the SAF 44 now.
